summary.headline: Greenply Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit record INR776.2 crore (+19.6% YoY) with core EBITDA margin of 12%, up 150 bps YoY.
summary.overview: Greenply reported its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR776.2 crore in Q4 FY26, with core EBITDA of INR93.2 crore at a 12% margin. MDF delivered its record quarter at INR189.4 crore revenue and 17% margin, while plywood volume grew 15.6% YoY. Management flagged a CEO/JMD resignation, a tax search operation, and a INR15.16 crore exceptional impairment linked to the Dubai entity, and guided to a 0.7-0.72 peak debt-to-equity during the MDF capex cycle. Part of Q4 volume growth was attributed to channel stocking in the second half of March, and chemical costs rose sharply, prompting price increases from April.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR588.5 crore, volume +15.6% and value +14.6% YoY, core EBITDA margin 10.4% (+120 bps YoY). FY26 revenue INR2,105.7 crore (+7.5%), volume +8.3%, margin 8.8%. Price hikes of 4-5% effective April 2026; management attributes gross margin dip to product mix.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 record revenue INR189.4 crore on 62,000 CBM (+45.3% volume YoY), margin 17%. FY26 revenue INR635.6 crore (+19.9%), margin 13.4%. Price increases of 5% and 10% effective April 2026 (15% total per analyst confirmation); FY27 volume guidance 25-30%.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales INR12.99 crore; FY26 revenue INR44.27 crore with PAT loss INR50.8 crore (Greenply share INR25.4 crore). Management expects breakeven around the middle of next year.

guidance_outlook: Plywood volume growth target of 10% for the rest of FY27, with margins held at recent levels contingent on volume delivery.
MDF volume growth of 25-30% in FY27, using near-full capacity; EBITDA margins to be kept consistent with recent performance (Q4 FY26 MDF margin 17% described as sustainable).
Management expects the March 2026 quarter consolidated margin to be the new norm, with H2 FY27 plywood margin upside from new process technology.
Peak debt-to-equity expected at 0.7-0.72 during FY27 or the year after, reverting to 0.5-0.6 the following year.
Effective tax rate around 22% (standalone 22%, subsidiaries around 17%).

Odisha plywood plant capex about INR130 crore; other plywood technology improvements about INR45-50 crore; MDF capex about INR425 crore, of which about INR300 crore falls in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28.
capex_capacity: PVC and WPC plant commenced commercial production in April 2026 with installed capacity of 6 million kg for doors and 3 million kg for door frames; peak revenue potential INR75-80 crore.
New MDF facility: civil construction underway and key machinery ordered; management says on track. About INR10 crore paid as advance to main equipment supplier so far.
Plywood greenfield facility (Odisha) under construction at full pace with major orders placed.

Plywood process change (ContiRoll technology): implemented in 2 of 4 existing facilities, remaining 2 to be done in FY27. Management says it lowers cost, manpower and material use and improves quality.
Flooring line in MDF expected to be fully operational in early Q2 FY27, with annual top-line capacity of about INR70-75 crore at peak.
Management says investment per cubic metre on the new Conti capacity is lower, aiming to improve capex turnover and ROCE. Steady-state ROCE aspiration of 18-20% at peak utilisation.
demand_pricing: Chemical prices rose over 50% early in the quarter; chemicals are about 30% of MDF raw material cost. Price increases: MDF 5% and 10% (15% total per analyst question confirmed by management) and plywood 4-5%, effective April 2026. Management says chemical prices have stabilised.

Q4 volume growth partly reflected channel stocking in the second half of March, plus a shift from unorganised to organised players as small MDF and plywood players were disrupted by cash-tight supplier terms.
Industry MDF growth estimated at 15-20% annualised; plywood industry growth 3-4%. Management estimates Greenply MDF market share about 7% currently, peaking at 8-8.5%.
Timber prices stable in Q4 and expected flat for FY27. Imports of MDF largely wiped out due to BIS and dollar/freight conditions.
Receivable days rose by about 3 days from December 2025 (analyst cited 47 to 54 days YoY), attributed to OEM growth and furniture factory business; management says receivables are LC-protected.
Advertising spend in Q4 lower YoY; management says the annual amount is unchanged and it is timing of expense recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Is MDF margin sustainable and is plywood double-digit margin sustainable with quality issues in the lower-end brand fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MDF margin is sustainable, driven by volume and operating leverage on fixed costs, with cost increases already passed on. Plywood margin is sustainable if volume targets are met; process changes have improved quality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet trajectory after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity may peak at 0.7-0.72 in one year, then return to 0.5-0.6 the following year; management does not want substantially higher debt.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-offs (Dubai/GMEL, forex) behind the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no further challenges, with all potential liability on equity, corporate guarantees and loan advances provided for in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume growth inflated by channel inventory, and does Q1 FY27 continue the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management partly agreed, noting some stocking in the second half of March, and attributed growth mainly to a shift from unorganised to organised players; Q1 FY27 has started strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and split of growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR425 crore MDF capex, roughly INR300 crore in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28; Odisha plywood about INR130 crore; plywood technology upgrades INR45-50 crore. Analyst estimated about INR480 crore for FY27, which management said was almost right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDF gross margin volatile and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q2 and Q3 volatility to line extension disruption and trading mix; Q4 FY26 margin is the base to deliver going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the income tax search conducted and is there any liability?
qa_highlights.answer: Search covered Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel; management said the reason is not known, no order or demand has been received, and the auditor has noted no liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the JMD and CEO Manoj Tulsian step down, and is there a change in strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: He stepped down to pursue personal commitments and will continue as an advisor; sales, plant, IT, HR and marketing heads are in place, and a full-time replacement at his level is not planned immediately.

risks_watch: Leadership transition: CEO/JMD Manoj Tulsian stepped down (advisory role retained); no full-time replacement at his level planned immediately, with Sanidhya Mittal leading the call.

Balance sheet: debt-to-equity guided to peak at 0.7-0.72 in FY27 or the year after (from 0.52 at Q4 FY26), with MDF capex of about INR425 crore (about INR300 crore FY27, INR125 crore FY28) plus Odisha plywood about INR130 crore.

Margin sustainability: MDF 17% and plywood 10.4% Q4 margins are guided as the base, but depend on delivering 10% plywood and 25-30% MDF volume growth; price hikes of 4-5% (plywood) and 5-10% (MDF) effective April 2026 and chemical costs (over 50% spike, about 30% of MDF raw material) remain watch items.

Volume quality: part of Q4 growth reflected channel stocking in the second half of March; receivable days rose about 3 days from December 2025 (analyst cited 47 to 54 days YoY) on OEM growth, with management saying receivables are LC-protected.

Tax and one-offs: income tax search (26 Feb to 2 Mar 2026) covering Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel has no demand or order yet; INR15.16 crore Dubai/GMEL exceptional impairment booked; management says no further liability expected.
Furniture & fittings JV: Q4 PAT loss INR13 crore (share INR6.5 crore); breakeven targeted around mid-next year, dependent on Phase 2 capex timing.

summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on MDF margins (17% sustainable, cost increases passed on) and on plywood volumes, with the call led by JMD Sanidhya Mittal after CEO Manoj Tulsian's resignation. Evasive or non-committal on the tax search reason, the JV breakeven timing, the exact plywood margin and tax-driven details, and on the exact market share and ROCE figures, where he said he could not give precise numbers.
